chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no harm if a person who cannot afford Hajj (al-sarurah) performs Hajj on behalf of another person who cannot afford it.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: A person who is poor and cannot afford the cost of Hajj
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a poor person perform Hajj on behalf of another poor person?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of Hajj al-Badal, specifically addressing the scenario where a poor individual (sarurah) performs Hajj on behalf of another poor person who cannot afford it themselves. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the financial capacity of the agent, ensuring the obligation is met even when resources are limited, provided the core conditions of validity are preserved.
